title: Enterprise AI
tagline: Platform, governance, and evaluation carry the weight — the model is rarely the hard part.

clusters.label: Platform
clusters.summary: The substrate every AI workload sits on.

clusters.label: AI systems
clusters.summary: The retrieval and orchestration patterns that make models useful.

clusters.label: Operations
clusters.summary: Keeping a deployed system honest over time.

nodes.label: Platform architecture
nodes.summary: The layers — data, feature, model, orchestration, application — and who owns each one.
keyPoints: Most enterprise AI failure is an integration failure, not a modelling failure.
Separate storage, compute, and semantics so each can be replaced independently.
Draw the ownership boundary before choosing the vendor.

resources.label: Choose the shape of a data platform

nodes.label: Data foundation
nodes.summary: Governed, contracted, reproducible data — the constraint that quietly caps every AI ambition.
keyPoints: Schema contracts turn producer/consumer arguments into a reviewable artefact.
Freshness and grain are AI requirements, not just analytics requirements.
If a number can't be reproduced, an AI answer built on it can't be defended.

nodes.label: Retrieval-augmented generation
nodes.summary: Ground a model's answer in retrieved, permissioned content instead of its own memory.
keyPoints: Retrieval quality sets the ceiling; generation only spends what retrieval provides.
Chunking, ranking, and citation are three separate problems with three separate metrics.
Permissions must be enforced at retrieval, never through prompt instructions.

nodes.label: Agents & orchestration
nodes.summary: Multi-step flows where a model calls tools, and something has to bound the loop.
keyPoints: Every tool call is an authorisation decision.
Bound steps, cost, and latency explicitly — autonomy without limits is an outage.
Deterministic routing beats a clever agent for most enterprise workflows.

resources.label: Cancellation with context
resources.note: Timeouts and clean shutdown for tool loops

nodes.label: Natural language to data
nodes.summary: Translate a question into a governed query, and show the query alongside the answer.
keyPoints: Restrict access at the data layer, not in the prompt.
Show the generated SQL so a reader can audit the answer.
Evaluate with ambiguous and adversarial questions, not just clean ones.

nodes.label: MLOps lifecycle
nodes.summary: Versioning, deployment, monitoring, and retraining as one continuous loop.
keyPoints: Version data, code, and model together or you cannot reproduce an incident.
Deployment is the midpoint of the lifecycle, not the finish line.
Retraining triggers should be written down before the first drift alarm.

nodes.label: Evaluation & monitoring
nodes.summary: Graded test sets offline, quality and cost signals online, and a path between them.
keyPoints: Build the evaluation set before the system — it defines what 'working' means.
Track groundedness and refusal behaviour, not only accuracy.
Log inputs, retrieved context, and outputs so regressions are diagnosable.

nodes.label: Reliability & cost
nodes.summary: Latency budgets, fallbacks, rate limits, and the unit economics of every call.
keyPoints: Model calls are a dependency with an SLO and a bill attached.
Design the degraded path: what does the product do when the model is unavailable?
Cost per resolved task is the metric that survives contact with finance.

nodes.label: Governance
nodes.summary: Who may see what, who approved this system, and what evidence exists that it behaves.
keyPoints: Access control belongs to the data platform, inherited by every AI surface.
Governance that arrives after launch becomes a rollback.
Evidence — lineage, evaluations, audit trails — is the deliverable, not the policy document.

nodes.label: Legibility & adoption
nodes.summary: People use a system they can inspect, correct, and predict.
keyPoints: Show sources and the reasoning path; hidden work is not trusted work.
An override mechanism raises adoption more than an accuracy point.
Adoption failures are usually workflow failures wearing a model costume.
